top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye for the optical lattice clock: magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, realised at roughly 1e-18 with independent reproduction at several institutes, so the result is mature and the two-name allocation fits the three-person limit. A citation naming the lattice architecture and the 1e-18 realisation keeps it distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a strong prediction-plus-experiment case that I ranked fourth at opening and place second here, ahead of no award. I prefer an award to P000 because the evidence supports at least one mature, correctly allocated prize.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for the slate: my profile records no relationship with Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp. My superconducting-circuit and WACQT conflict concerned B024, which is not on this slate.
